Christmas Light Tours Phoenix: See Holiday Displays in Style

Planning a holiday lights evening around the Valley? This is planning guidance, not a tour package. The displays are run by other organizations, each with its own dates, hours, ticketing and parking, and those change from season to season — check the organizer's own current page before you plan an evening around it.

What we provide is the transportation: a private chauffeured vehicle for the evening, booked by the hour.

ZooLights at the Phoenix Zoo

This is the one display we publish sourced, current details for. From the Zoo's official ZooLights page, checked September 15, 2026:

  • Season: November 25, 2026 – January 15, 2027
  • Hours: 5:30–10:30 pm
  • Ages: all ages
  • Admission: standard admission is valid for one public night in the season, and the current page does not require a timed-entry ticket
  • Ticket sales: members from September 17, 2026; general sales from October 1, 2026

It is primarily a walking visit, and most animals are not visible at night. Dates, hours and ticketing are the Zoo's to change, so check its page before you buy or plan.

A sensory-friendly night and a drive-through night are ticketed separately and run under their own rules.

Other Valley displays

Neighborhood displays, lake events and downtown light walks each publish their own schedule, and hours, ticketing and parking change from year to year. Check the current official schedule for the display you want, then send us the addresses and the times you want to be at each one. We build the evening around what you have confirmed with the venue.

How the transportation works

One hourly charter covers the evening: pickup at your address or a single staging address, the drive out, the wait while you are at the display, and the return to the addresses on the reservation. Stops inside the hours you have reserved cost nothing extra, because that time is already booked.

What it is not: we are not affiliated with any venue or event organizer, and we do not sell, hold or include admission, tickets or parking. There is no holiday package and no package price.

The written quote is built from the vehicle you choose and the hours you reserve. Reserving more hours can change the price, so confirm the duration in writing rather than assuming it is the same either way. The four-hour minimum applies to every vehicle except the 56-passenger motorcoach, which is five.

Where a vehicle of your size may stop, and how close that is to an entrance, is the venue's call on the night rather than something we can promise in advance.

Planning the evening

  • Count everyone who has to ride together first, then count what they are bringing. Passenger capacity is a seating limit, not cargo space, and strollers, folding wagons, coats and camp chairs all take seats or luggage room.
  • Send mobility and accessibility needs with the request — a wheelchair, a walker, a folding mobility scooter, a low step, or a rider who cannot manage a long walk from wherever the vehicle is allowed to stop. Vehicles differ and it changes which one fits.
  • Work the hours out from your own evening: outbound travel from your pickup address, a buffer to get everyone in, the visit itself, and the return.
  • Venue rules and vehicle rules are separate. Each display sets its own; ours are on the ride rules page.

Get a quote

Tell us the night, the pickup address, the rider count, what the group is bringing and any mobility needs, and we will confirm the vehicle and the price in writing before anything is reserved.
